hook: Brain fog and depression share overlapping biology — which is why fixing one often improves the other
topic: Neuroinflammation as a shared mechanism in fog and low mood
body:
**Brain fog and depression share overlapping biological mechanisms. This is not a loose analogy — it reflects measurable similarities in the inflammatory and neurotransmitter profiles of both states. And it explains something that often confuses people: why fixing the biology sometimes improves both, regardless of which label you're using.**

One of those shared mechanisms is neuroinflammation — low-grade inflammatory signalling within the brain that impairs the efficiency of neural transmission. Elevated inflammatory markers have been found in people with both major depression and in people experiencing chronic cognitive fog without a mood disorder diagnosis.

The inputs that drive neuroinflammation — disrupted sleep, ultra-processed diet, sedentary behaviour, chronic psychological stress — are also the inputs that correlate most strongly with both conditions.

This does not mean brain fog is depression, or that lifestyle changes are a substitute for clinical treatment when clinical treatment is warranted. It means the biology has more overlap than the separate labels suggest.

If you're experiencing persistent cognitive fog, it is worth asking whether the same inputs that are degrading your thinking might also be affecting your mood — and whether addressing the biology serves both.
